gaps.sentence: The drug is remarkably effective. ___, it has almost no side effects.
gaps.explanation: 'Furthermore' introduces an additional point supporting the same claim.

gaps.sentence: Scarcely had she opened the letter ___ she burst into tears.
gaps.explanation: 'Scarcely... when' marks the immediate consequence of the first event.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: He didn't whisper the news; ___, he announced it to the whole office.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' corrects the first statement with its opposite.

gaps.sentence: We took the coast road ___ the motorway to enjoy the views.
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of + noun' marks the rejected alternative.

gaps.sentence: We went for a long walk ___ it was drizzling.
gaps.explanation: Only the conjunction 'even though' can introduce the finite clause 'it was drizzling'.

gaps.sentence: He had hardly stepped off the plane ___ he was rushed into a meeting.
She speaks fluent Mandarin; ___, she reads classical Chinese.
gaps.explanation: 'Moreover' adds a further, even more remarkable achievement.
